note: Friday 07:00 SGT re-verify (pre-Asia-open) against the Thu 23 Jul US close. The melt-up cracked into an oil-shock risk-off: Brent topped $100 intraday (WTI ~$90) after Houthi tanker strikes and a collapsed ceasefire, 10Y hit a year-high ~4.62%, and equities sold off led by mega-cap tech (S&P -1.2% to 7,408, Nasdaq -2.2% to 25,138; Alphabet -7%, Tesla -14%). Sentiment sits in FEAR (CNN ~43, crypto 31); longer-term breadth stayed broad (~69% of the S&P >200-DMA into the day) but the selloff was a sharp one-day narrowing concentrated in tech. Fear&Greed is fetched LIVE in-browser with the baked value as fallback; breadth & regional flows are researched daily (no free real-time API). CNN's component API returned HTTP 418 again this run, so the 7 sub-readings are INFERRED from the ~43 composite and sourced internals and labeled as such.

components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index fell -1.2% to 7,408 on 23 Jul but still sits above a rising 125- and 200-DMA after the summer run — momentum cooled toward neutral on the oil-shock selloff. [Inferred — CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run]

components.name: Stock Price Strength

components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). ~69% of the S&P sat above its 200-DMA into the day (best since February), but the -2.2% Nasdaq selloff narrowed near-term volume-breadth — moderating from greedy toward neutral. [Inferred — mcoscillator]

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options demand rose as the oil shock and equity drop drove a hedging bid — a fearful tilt consistent with the sub-45 composite. [Inferred]

breadth.note: Breadth was broad going into the 23 Jul oil-shock selloff — ~69% of S&P members above their 200-DMA (near best since February) — but the down-day (S&P -1.2%, Nasdaq -2.2%) was a sharp near-term narrowing concentrated in tech/growth (Alphabet -7%, Tesla -14%) while Energy led on Brent >$100. That is a longer-term-broad / short-term-narrowing split against low-40s Fear sentiment. Several sub-metrics (50-DMA %, daily A/D, net new highs, McClellan) are approximate or lagged as labeled. The open question into the 28-29 Jul FOMC: whether the oil/yield shock deepens the narrowing or resolves as another rotation.

flows.period: ICI week ended 8 Jul 2026 (long-term MF+ETF) plus BofA 'Flow Show'/EPFR early-mid July. Flows lag ~2-6 days and PRE-DATE the 23 Jul oil-shock selloff — read the positioning theme, not any single number. Labeled EARLY/MID-JULY 2026.
flows.narrative: The freshest verifiable weekly read (through ~8 Jul, pre-selloff) was risk-on at the margin: ICI reported +$66.1bn of total long-term inflows with equity funds pulling +$42.85bn — a sharp swing from -$10.2bn the prior week. On the BofA private-client/EPFR tape US equities logged their first net inflow in five weeks (hedge-fund-led) with record Consumer-Discretionary inflows and the largest Financials outflows, while buybacks slid to a 6-week low and EM debt funds have drawn >$60bn YTD. The positioning picture was stretched/greedy into the 23 Jul oil shock — so next week's Flow Show is the tell for whether the energy scare reverses the equity re-entry. Per-region weekly detail (Europe/DM, China, Japan, cash, gold) was not itemized in retrievable free sources this run.
